look_here_first: Look for slender prostrate to suberect prairie plants with very NARROW or linear leaflets. Small heads often have 4–12 flowers; mature pods are long, nearly straight and slender (about 35–70 × 2–3 mm), unlike the wide sickle pods of D. illinoensis.

key_traits.label: Growth flower fruit
key_traits.text: Low spreading perennial of prairie and open ground, including mowed grass, rocky/clayey sites; stems can extend about 60–100 cm. Leaflets very narrow. 5 stamens rather than the 10-stamen heads of D. velutinus. Pods narrow and nearly straight.

key_traits.label: Distinguishing characters
key_traits.text: Compared with Illinois bundleflower: small few-flowered heads and longer narrower almost straight pods; Illinois has big heads and sharply falcate wide pods. Compared with velutinus: 5 vs 10 stamens and often less visibly velvety stems.

key_traits.label: Shared genus
key_traits.text: Unarmed perennial Fabaceae with compound bipinnate leaves and small brushlike heads, often a petiolar/rachis gland, flat legume pods. Pod structure diagnostic.
